newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backed spreads widen, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backed spreads widen, trade thin.

text.p: Light mortgage-banker selling on Friday kept higher-coupon U.S. mortgage-backed securities from breaking through the positive threshold, mortgage experts said.
Although discount coupons managed to notch a couple of ticks higher, current coupons and premiums flirted with par levels most of the afternoon.
Yield spreads over Treasuries were moderately wider in spots and trading was relatively thin as many players were still off on holiday, traders said.
"I heard there was some mortgage-banker selling earlier in the day," said one New York-based trader who did not know the volume sold.
Another trader said he had also heard about the selling, but he conceded that very little activity occurred otherwise.
"We're seeing very little today," he said. "It's been extremely quiet yesterday and today."
By late afternoon, the market traded flat to 1/32 higher in most coupons.
Specifically, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent pass-throughs were 1/32 higher at 99-17/32, yielding 113 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were also up 1/32, at 99-15/32 and 99-19/32, respectively.
The 10-year Treasury note advanced 1/32 at 99-29/32 to yield 6.51 percent.
